Cloud RDMA and direct storage access

What customers and partners are saying

"Nutanix is committed to helping organizations run their applications and data anywhere. Bringing Nutanix Cloud Clusters (NC2) to Google Cloud's new Z4M metal instances reflects that mission and our continued partnership with Google Cloud. By combining Z4M’s exceptional I/O performance and high storage density along with Intel’s advanced compute and AMX-driven efficiency, NC2 on Z4M provides the scale, density, and performance required to power everything from dense VDI clusters to demanding, data-intensive AI workloads."- Saveen Pakala, Vice President of Product Management, Nutanix

"Google's Z4M VMs bring Cloud RDMA to a storage-optimized VM with much higher local SSD density than previous generations. In our testing, Cloud RDMA on Z4M demonstrated outstanding performance with up to 3.7x lower latency and up to 6x lower CPU usage than TCP. For our customers, that means faster, more predictable performance across a wide variety of use cases, from I/O-intensive databases to analytics and AI workloads, with the storage density to scale capacity efficiently."Adik Sokolovski, Chief R&D Officer, Silk

“We're excited to support Google Cloud's new Z4M platform as part of the Sycomp Intelligent Data Storage Platform. With greater capacity per node and the continued evolution of the Z-series architecture, Z4M helps customers achieve new levels of performance and efficiency. Supporting innovations like Z4M reinforces Sycomp's commitment to delivering high-performance storage solutions across the Google Cloud ecosystem.”- Scott Fadden, Senior HPC Solutions Architect, Sycomp

"We've worked alongside Google Cloud for years on the most demanding AI and machine learning workloads. In our testing, we found the new Z4M machines deliver roughly twice the read throughput and up to 79% more IOPS, generation over generation (Z3 family). This means more data, more tokens, and more finished work. We’re excited to see what our joint customers build with these powerful machines."- Ajay Singh, Chief Product Officer, WEKA

items.title: Highlights and reflections from Google Public Sector Summit: Where mission meets moonshot
items.author: Katharyn WhiteDirector of Marketing, Public SectorGoogle Cloud
items.content:
Over government leaders, innovators, and industry partners convened across two-days at our Google Public Sector Summit in Washington D.C. where we explored the theme, “Where mission meets moonshot.” We were honored to bring together leaders who are driving impact in the agentic era and leveraging agents to help boost productivity, drive innovation, and transform how services are delivered.

Let’s take a closer look at the sessions, speakers, demos, and activations throughout the event that showcased how leaders across education and government are collaborating with Google Public Sector to turn their moonshot aspirations into secure, scaled, real-world mission outcomes.

In our morning keynote, CEO of Google Public Sector, unpacked the event theme and shared how organizations like NASA, NOAA, The Department of War, The Department of Energy, The State of Connecticut, The U.S. Army, Case Western Reserve University, and more are collaborating with Google to drive impact in the agentic era. Karen underscored the importance of leading boldly, building with and for your people, and scaling for impact.

, Field CTO of Google Public Sector, shared a live product demonstration that showcased Google’s technology in action. Attendees had the opportunity to hear from leaders , Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment, and Administrator for the General Services Administration, who shared how they are applying technology to transform their missions and power their moonshots. Through partnership and powerful technology, we are creating impact at scale by transforming services, strengthening security, and improving outcomes.

Dedicated programming for the agentic era

During our Cloud Talks session, attendees heard from Managing Director of Customer Engineering for Google Public Sector, as she hosted a series of talks across critical pillars of public sector transformation. Presentations highlighted infrastructure for the agentic era led by VP/GM for Accelerated Computing Systems at Google Cloud; building safely with Google’s agentic capabilities led by , VP of Product Management for Gemini; and implementing proactive defense at planet-scale led by , VP of Google Threat Intelligence.

Attendees also heard from dozens of customer and partner speakers during our breakout panels hosted by Google Public Sector leaders Ron Bushar, Tony Orlando, and as well as our lightning talks and closed-door birds of a feather discussions on topics including tokenomics, migration, and compliance. Alongside our customers and partners, we showcased how agents are transforming every facet of the public sector, from accelerating scientific breakthroughs, advancing healthcare outcomes, improving service delivery, strengthening national security, and more.

Over the course of the event, we offered specialized programming and engagement opportunities for national security and defense leaders. Through our Partner Connect programming, we shared how we are scaling our impact through a thriving, highly capable partner community and introduced enhanced partner initiatives focused on fostering deeper collaboration, supercharging frontline adoption, and expanding mission delivery capabilities across our valued partner network.

Hands-on innovation with Google Public Sector

The Mission Exchange served as our interactive showfloor centerpiece, bringing multi-agent coordination to life with our flagship Emergency Response Simulation, as well as live demos that showcased our full-stack innovations encompassing everything from planet-scale infrastructure to leading models and agentic platforms.

We hosted 19 lightning talks in the Mission Exchange, featuring customer, partner and Google experts who shared live demos and showcased real-world mission-ready solutions. Attendees also had the opportunity to join our technical hands-on labs including “Getting Started with Gemini” and “Build Gemini Agents: From Prompt to Prototype” where they built functional mission-ready agents with Google Cloud.

I was honored to lead our closing session, where we brought together visionary leaders (The White House), (NYS Board of Elections), and (USPTO) to explore practical strategies for fostering a culture of courageous problem-solving and applying technology to supercharge ambition and ingenuity in entirely new ways.

As we look ahead, I want to leave you with one question:

Answering this question will require bold leadership, ambition, and courage; it will require partnership and collaboration across teams and organizations; and technology that can help amplify capacity and potential. Leading in the agentic era means being comfortable with stepping into the unknown. It means asking and answering audacious questions, expanding the boundaries of what’s possible, and taking one small step in a bold new direction - even when - when it is hard.

Let’s build what’s next, together

We believe that bold moonshots all start with a single, pragmatic first step. To help you get started, I encourage you to take advantage of a number of helpful resources and opportunities to engage:

  • Request a demo to see how Wiz Agents can help your agency meet today’s security demands at machine speed.
  • Schedule a 1:1 consultation with a Google team member or reach us at geminiforgov@google.com.

The agentic era will not be defined by what technology can do, but by what we choose to build with it. Let’s go build, together.

items.title: Chrome Enterprise Premium drives 50%+ projected cost reduction for Mercari
items.author: Yu SusakiManager of Enterprise SecurityMercari
items.content:
Flexibility and security with one secure enterprise browser

Previously, our customer service environment relied on a mix of legacy devices routed through VDI. This created operational friction, a frustrating user experience, increased IT overhead, and required managing overlapping DLP controls on both the VDI and local environments to prevent potential data transfer between the two. To simplify our architecture, we decided to shift focus from OS-level isolation to browser-layer data control, introducing Chrome Enterprise Premium and Chromebooks to a partner environment to establish data control and boundaries based on user actions.

By leveraging Chrome Enterprise Premium, our team configured strict DLP rules, implementing controls to restrict users from pasting or uploading files to destinations outside of Mercari's approved business tools. This helps protect sensitive company data from being leaked or fed into unapproved channels. We knew investing in Chrome Enterprise Premium would help enable AI-powered productivity while restricting data leaks to unsanctioned AI tools. The transition was smooth because our workforce was already using the Chrome Enterprise browser across the company prior to the security upgrade. Because employees were able to continue using the browser interface they were already accustomed to, the implementation of the new security solution was easier and resulted in strong user adoption. By implementing these policy controls, we could confidently adopt new AI capabilities while ensuring enterprise data boundaries are strictly enforced.

Beyond DLP, transitioning to this new architecture dramatically streamlined IT operations and reduced costs. With zero-touch enrollment, IT no longer needs to manually set up individual devices before handing them to users. Furthermore, by reducing dependency on VDI and consolidating various security agents (like legacy DLP, MDM, and EDR), we project a cost reduction of more than 50% over a three-year period within this environment, covering device costs, VDI running costs, and security licenses.

Additionally, this browser-centric model eliminates the heavy operational overhead and specialized engineering resources traditionally required just to maintain a complex VDI infrastructure, allowing us to redirect valuable IT talent to higher-priority initiatives.

Implementing Chrome Enterprise Premium and ChromeOS enabled a zero-trust, device-based approach that protects data, slashes IT costs, and measurably improves security. We eliminated VDI friction, lowered costs, and strictly enforced data boundaries—ultimately making Chrome Enterprise Premium the right move to deeply protect our marketplace and users.

Looking ahead, we are set up as an AI-forward organization that wants its employees to benefit from new technologies, like agentic browsers, but in a highly controlled environment. To achieve this, we leveraged the power of Chrome Enterprise Premium. As a first step, we are using browser policies to enable a safe, read-only adoption of Gemini in Chrome. Employees can now leverage multi-page context and seamless side-panel interactions without manual copy-pasting, which drastically reduces the risk of unintended actions like data modification. Looking forward, we plan to continuously explore the optimal balance between AI productivity and security. By dynamically utilizing both existing and upcoming enterprise security features alongside Chrome Enterprise Premium’s robust DLP, we will ensure data boundaries evolve proactively, empowering our workforce to innovate safely.
